title: Shoosmiths offers £1m bonus pot for 1 million AI prompts
author: Shoosmiths · David Jackson

kp.k: Firmwide bonus rewards quantified AI adoption
kp.d: In its 2 April 2025 press release, Shoosmiths announces an annual target of one million Microsoft Copilot prompts in its new financial year, unlocking £1m for staff if achieved. This is one element of its multi-million collegiate bonus pool, available to all staff. The firm claims to be the first major law firm to link a firmwide bonus to workforce AI use; the release describes an incentive and target, not an achieved outcome.
qs: Shoosmiths has reinforced its position at the forefront of legal innovation by becoming the first major law firm to link a firmwide bonus to the use of artificial intelligence (AI) by its workforce.
The firm has set a clear and ambitious annual target: one million Microsoft Copilot prompts to unlock a £1m bonus pot for staff in its new financial year.
The bonus metric will form one element of the firm’s multi-million collegiate bonus pool, available to all staff.

kp.d: Shoosmiths states that four Copilot uses per colleague per working day would comfortably exceed the annual target. It plans transparent firmwide usage tracking and monthly updates to encourage collaboration, learning and momentum.
qs: If every Shoosmiths colleague uses Copilot just four times per working day, the one million prompt target will be comfortably exceeded.
Usage will be tracked and shared transparently across the firm, with monthly updates to encourage collaboration, learning and momentum.

kp.k: CEO frames AI as augmentation rather than replacement
kp.d: CEO David Jackson asserts that AI will not replace the firm's people but will free time for problem-solving, trust-building and supporting clients through complexity. The release frames AI as augmenting lawyers' and business teams' judgement, creativity and insight, rather than substituting for them. These are the firm's stated expectations and positioning.
qs: We don’t fear AI—it won’t replace our people. Instead, it frees them to spend more time on the human-to-human work that really matters: solving problems, building trust, and supporting clients through complexity.

Through a combination of training, peer support, and financial incentives, the firm is embedding many forms of AI into how its people work—augmenting the judgement, creativity and insight of its talented lawyers and business teams with powerful new digital tools.

kp.k: AI rollout combines partnership, training and peer learning
kp.d: Shoosmiths describes its Microsoft partnership and early adoption of Copilot across operations as underpinning the initiative. Its engagement programme includes drop-in sessions, practical workshops and an internal knowledge hub for sharing use cases, tips and success stories.
qs: The initiative is underpinned by the firm’s partnership with Microsoft as an early adopter of Copilot across Shoosmiths’ operations.

AI rollout at Shoosmiths is supported by a wide-ranging engagement programme, including drop-in sessions, hands-on workshops, and an internal knowledge hub where teams share practical use cases, tips, and success stories.

kp.k: New innovation and data roles support organisational change
kp.d: The firm reports that roles emerging to support the AI shift include Innovation Leads in each Division, Head of Legal Innovation and a new Data Manager. It presents these as long-term investment in digital capability and its people, alongside a qualitative claim that AI is already improving efficiency and client delivery.
qs: The firm is already seeing the positive impact of AI on both efficiency and client delivery.

New roles are emerging to support this shift, including Innovation Leads in each Division, Head of Legal Innovation and a new Data Manager, reflecting Shoosmiths’ long-term investment in digital capability and its people.

kp.k: Client benefits are the stated purpose beyond prompt counts
kp.d: Although the announced bonus metric is usage volume, Jackson emphasises quality of use and client benefits as the initiative's purpose. He presents tools, room to explore and collective encouragement as ways to improve client service.
qs: This is not just about how many times someone uses AI—it’s about how well we use it and the benefits it will have for our clients,
We’re giving our people the tools, the space and the encouragement to explore what’s possible—together.

kp.k: AI emissions enter the firm's sustainability plans
kp.d: Shoosmiths links AI adoption to its commitment to net zero by 2040 and says it is on track against its science-based goals. It announces a new sustainability approach in 2025 that includes managing upstream emissions from AI and other purchased goods and services.
qs: Shoosmiths is also committed to sustainable innovation and achieving net zero by 2040, in line with our science-based goals, and is on track to do so.
This includes taking action to manage our upstream emissions from AI and other goods and services with a new approach to sustainability in 2025.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Shoosmiths presents financially incentivised AI adoption as a means of improving client service; CEO David Jackson predicts augmentation rather than replacement of its people.
pts.d: The firm's 2 April 2025 press release claims it is the first major law firm to link a firmwide bonus to workforce AI use. It announces an annual target of one million Microsoft Copilot prompts to unlock a £1 million staff bonus pot, intended to embed AI in everyday work and improve client value. Jackson says AI can improve the speed and quality of client results and will free staff for problem-solving, trust-building and supporting clients through complexity rather than replace them. The firm also reports that AI is already improving efficiency and client delivery, and that new innovation and data roles are emerging to support the shift. These are claims about Shoosmiths' operations and ambitions, not demonstrated profession-wide effects.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source offers firm-reported experience, implementation details and CEO expectations, but no quantified evidence of service improvements or employment effects.
pts.d: Shoosmiths supports its account with its early adoption of Microsoft Copilot, training and peer-support arrangements, and the emergence of named innovation and data roles. Its statement that efficiency and client delivery are already improving is not accompanied by measured time savings, client outcomes or specific case studies. Jackson's non-replacement and superior-service claims are expressed as leadership assurances and expectations. The prompt target and bonus amount specify the adoption incentive, not measured productivity or quality gains. No comparative evidence is supplied for the first-major-law-firm claim.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The bonus is conditional on an annual usage target in the firm's new financial year; benefits are described as both already occurring and expected from continuing adoption.
pts.d: Published on 2 April 2025, the release places the one-million-prompt target in Shoosmiths' new financial year, without specifying its exact dates. The £1 million payout depends on achieving that target. The firm says four Copilot uses per colleague per working day would comfortably exceed it and promises monthly usage updates. Training, peer support and financial encouragement are presented as mechanisms supporting adoption. Jackson qualifies the initiative's purpose as effective use and client benefits, although the stated bonus trigger is prompt volume. His assurance that AI will not replace the firm's people has no explicit time horizon.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The claimed effects concern Shoosmiths' entire workforce, its lawyers and business teams, emerging innovation roles, and its clients.
pts.d: All staff are eligible for the collegiate bonus pool, and all colleagues are encouraged to contribute to the collective usage target. Lawyers and business teams are described as receiving tools that augment judgement, creativity and insight, with more time available for human interaction and complex client support. Innovation Leads, a Head of Legal Innovation and a Data Manager are identified as roles supporting the change. Clients are the intended beneficiaries of faster, better service. The release does not identify particular practice areas or client segments, or claim effects on access to justice or the wider legal labour market.
